title: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Designed organisms moved as simulated when upright, much less when inverted

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: For at least one deciliated, cardiac-muscle-powered design, the upright organisms' direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations, and inverting the design significantly reduced net displacement both in silico and in vivo.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Kriegman S 2020, A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms › Results › Locomotion.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: More specifically, the upright organisms’ direction of movement matched that of the in silico design under random perturbations (P < 0.01; details in SI Appendix, section S9), and inverting the design significantly reduced its net displacement both in silico (P < 0.001) and in vivo (P < 0.0001).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J, “A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms”, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (2020), doi:10.1073/pnas.1910837117; section “Results › Locomotion.”. Scope: Deciliated Xenopus reconfigurable organisms with cardiac tissue, compared with their simulated designs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2020-xenobots-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The variables and contrasts are explicit and strongly discriminating for the narrow result. The public paper and supplement support reanalysis of reported measurements, but full independent verification depends on access to raw trajectories.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recompute movement direction and net displacement for upright and inverted simulated and living designs, testing directional concordance and the inversion contrasts with the reported statistics.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw individual-level trajectories may not all be downloadable.

The claim concerns at least one selected design, limiting generalization.

fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.82
operationalizability: 0.98
data existence: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Heading and net displacement under an inversion control are standard kinematic variables, and the simulator that produced the in silico p-values is public. The living comparison rests on published statistics from one design without an open track file, so the in vivo clause cannot be remeasured. Re-simulation can confirm or refute the computational half.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For the reported deciliated cardiac design, compare net displacement and heading of upright versus inverted organisms in the simulator and, where tracks exist, in the living builds; the claim holds if upright heading matches the design and inversion reduces displacement in both.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The quantitative claim is for at least one design, so a re-run has to recover that design rather than a new evolutionary sample.

In vivo p-values are published, but the trial-level movement tracks are not deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.7
data existence: 0.6
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.85
